true_answer: 1.1. Additive and Multiplicative Principles 65 be | A ∩ B | . So perhaps we guess, | A ∪ B | | | A | + | B |−| A ∩ B | . This works for this one example. Will it always work? Think about what we are doing here. We want to know how many things are either in A or B (or both). We can throw in everything in A , and everything in B . This would give | A | + | B | many elements. But of course when you actually take the union, you do not repeat elements that are in both.
